links.comparator_used: Practicing neurologists (290 respondents); the study also ran ChatGPT-4o without RAG, but the abstract reports no numbers for that arm
links.outcome: Guideline-adherent decision-making at item level across 21 clinical vignettes
links.effect: 80.5% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.001 for ChatGPT-4o with RAG vs neurologists. Multivariable GEE odds ratio for ChatGPT-4o as predictor of evidence-based decision-making was 3.17 (95% CI 2.05-4.88; p < 0.0001).
links.tradeoff: Performance was no better than neurologists in emerging biomarker scenarios (e.g., serum neurofilament light chain) where clinical consensus is still evolving.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4o with RAG achieved significantly higher guideline adherence in decision-making than neurologists (80.5% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.001).
